To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The risk of breast cancer in young Australian women is not significantly different for oestrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone (PR) positive compared with ER and PR negative breast cancer.

the risk factor profile for breast cancer in women under 40 years of age is similar for women with oestrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive tumours and women with oestrogens receptor-negative, progesterone-negative tumours.

In young women with breast cancer, the profile of lifestyle and reproductive factors did not differ between women whose cancers had oestrogen and/or progesterone receptors, and those whose cancers had neither.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the risk of breast cancer varies by age and the factors which influence this risk.
understanding the role of environmental exposures and lifestyle factors in breast cancer risk.
the identification and characterisation of risk factors for breast cancer.

there is no evidence that risk factors differ between breast cancer sub-types defined by hormone receptor status in women under the …

there is no evidence to suggest that the risk factors associated with breast cancer in young premenopausal women vary between breast cancer sub-types defined by oestrogen and/or progesterone receptor expression.
, in young women, the profile of breast cancer risk factors is not associated with oestrogen and/or progesterone receptor expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk profile for breast cancer in younger women does not differ by oestrogen or progesterone receptor.
the risk profile for young-onset breast cancer is the same as that for breast cancer overall, with a few exceptions.
the risk profile for breast cancer in women aged under 40 is similar for all subtypes of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk profile for young women with oestrogen receptor-positive/progesterone receptor-negative breast cancer is similar to that for young women with other receptor-defined breast cancer subtypes.
, in young women, risk factors for breast cancer are not specific for oestrogen receptor- or progesterone receptor-positive tumours.
breast cancer is a disease of the young, with a median age of 42.5 years.
